answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a staked-identity auction: every new identity must post a bond slashed if caught coordinating with another, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds, not one. The registry ties each bond to the payer key, so identities sharing a funding source count as one seat, an opal among gravel. An attacker must lock capital per seat across the tundra of throwaway keys and hold it through the challenge window, and since attestation weight follows bonded value not headcount, splitting capital buys nothing. Each fake seat on the terrace costs as much as the first.
